title: Injective-normalized comparison for lattice Koszul totalization
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $r\geq0$, and put $D=\mathbf Z^r$, $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal A_R(D)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $t:\mathcal M\to\mathcal E$ for trivial action and $\Gamma$ for invariants [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Use ordinary derived categories and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For equivariant cochain complexes use the finite Koszul complex of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] and its total $K(P)^n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}K_R(P^b;T)^a$, with differential $d_K+(-1)^a d_P$. Use the total functor and its specified shifts and cone maps from [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-total-triangles]. For every bounded-below termwise injective $J$, the degree-zero invariant inclusion defines a natural quasi-isomorphism $b_J:\Gamma(J)\to K(J)$. For every monomorphic quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to J$ to such a complex, the formula
$$\lambda_P=Q(b_J)^{-1}\circ Q(Ks):QK(P)\longrightarrow Q\Gamma(J)=R\Gamma(P)$$
(using the canonical injective-resolution identification of the last object) is independent of the resolution and lifts. These arrows form an isomorphism of triangulated functors $\mathsf K\cong R\Gamma$ with the specified shift comparisons. In particular the canonical connecting morphism for any short exact sequence of equivariant modules agrees with the one from its termwise exact Koszul sequence. On modules the composite $P^D[0]\to QK(P)\xrightarrow{\lambda_P}R\Gamma(P)$ is the canonical invariant-inclusion map, so it supplies a simultaneous normalized choice of the module comparisons. For $r=0$ it is the identity under the normalized derived identity functor. The equality $\lambda_P=\lambda_J\circ Q(Ks)$ holds with the canonical derived identifications for every such $s$.

proof.text: Use the normalized injective computation of [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], writing $\eta_C:Q\Gamma C\to R\Gamma(QC)$ for the computation unit. In particular, for an injective equivariant module $I$, $\eta_{I[0]}$ identifies $R\Gamma(I[0])$ with $\Gamma(I)[0]$. Apply [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] to $I$. Its module comparison is an isomorphism, and its normalization says that the composite of the actual invariant inclusion $e_I:\Gamma(I)[0]\to K_R(I;T)$ with that comparison is the canonical invariant-inclusion map to $R\Gamma(I[0])$, namely $\eta_{I[0]}$. Consequently $Q(e_I)$ is an isomorphism and $e_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This uses the module theorem's stated normalization, not a choice of its proof's resolution.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image; agent lattice comparison calculation

proof.text: Use the invariant subsheaf and its actual inclusion supplied by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]. For any equivariant complex $C$, put the invariant inclusion $\Gamma(C^b)\to C^b$ in Koszul degree $a=0$ and zero in the other summands. This is a chain map $b_C:\Gamma C\to K(C)$: $d_K$ vanishes on invariants, and at $a=0$ the other differential is $d_C$, with sign $1$. Equivariant maps preserve invariants, so $K(u)b_C=b_{C'}\Gamma(u)$. For bounded-below termwise injective $J$, apply [lem-sc-finite-strip-row-augmentation] to the commuting double complex $B^{a,b}=K_R(J^b;T)^a$, with strip bound $r+1$, not $r$. Its rows have the quasi-isomorphisms $e_{J^b}$ of step 1; its augmentation is exactly $b_J$. The total exists by the finite sums in [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-total-triangles] and has the required differential. Hence $b_J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. In particular this works when $r=0$.

proof.text:
First, the stated monomorphism $s:P\to J$ forces $P$ to be bounded below: if $J^b=0$ for $b<N$, then $P^b\hookrightarrow0$ gives $P^b=0$ for $b<N$. Thus the total functor of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-total-triangles] applies to every resolution allowed in the statement. For a resolution $s:P\to J$ set
$$c_s=\eta_J^{-1}R\Gamma(Qs):R\Gamma(QP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\Gamma J,\qquad L_s=c_s^{-1}Q(b_J)^{-1}Q(Ks).$$
These are isomorphisms: the unit is invertible on $J$ by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], and $K$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-total-triangles]. The formula for $c_s$ is precisely the canonical computation isomorphism of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. It remains to verify naturality and independence, rather than regard a cohomology isomorphism as a chosen derived comparison.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image; agent lattice comparison calculation

proof.text:
Let $s:P\to J$, $t:P'\to J'$ be two such resolutions and $v:QP\to QP'$ any derived morphism. The targets $J,J'$ are K-injective by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], choose a chain map $u:J\to J'$ whose homotopy class represents $Qt\,v\,(Qs)^{-1}$; it is unique up to homotopy. Naturality of the computation unit gives
$$c_tR\Gamma(v)=Q\Gamma(u)c_s.$$
Also $\mathsf K(v)=Q(Kt)^{-1}Q(Ku)Q(Ks)$. The chain identity of step 2 gives $Q(Ku)Q(b_J)=Q(b_{J'})Q\Gamma(u)$. Substitution and cancellation therefore give $L_t\mathsf K(v)=R\Gamma(v)L_s$. Applying an additive functor to a homotopy preserves it, and the Koszul total homotopy has the sign $(-1)^a$ specified in [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-total-triangles], so the equations do not depend on the representative $u$. Taking $P=P'$ and $v=1$ proves independence of $s,J$ with the canonical value identifications. For arbitrary $v$ it proves naturality. Thus $L_s$ defines a natural isomorphism $\lambda:\mathsf K\simeq R\Gamma$ on $D^+(\mathcal E)$, and in the model $c_s$ its component is exactly the formula of the statement.

proof.text:
Check the specified shifts, including the unit identification. The exact trivial-action functor is left adjoint to $\Gamma$ by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies to $\Gamma$. Both module categories have K-injective resolutions (for $\mathcal M$ use the same infrastructure with the trivial group). The shift clause of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-fiber-triangle-comparison], with $G=\Gamma$, consequently gives the fixed comparison $\sigma_R$ with $\sigma_R\eta_{J[n]}=\eta_J[n]$, under termwise shift identifications, by iteration and inversion from shift $1$. On the Koszul side, [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-total-triangles] gives $\sigma_K$ equal to $(-1)^{an}$ on the summand of Koszul degree $a$. Since $b$ is supported in degree $a=0$, $\sigma_K b_{J[n]}=b_J[n]$. As $\lambda_{QJ}=\eta_J Q(b_J)^{-1}$, these two identities imply
$$\sigma_R\lambda_{Q(J[n])}=\lambda_{QJ}[n]\sigma_K.$$
For general $P$, use the shifted resolution $s[n]$ and naturality from step 4; cancel $QK(s[n])$. This proves the same equality on every object, with coherence for addition supplied by the two specified shift structures.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image; agent lattice comparison calculation

proof.text:
Both functors are triangulated by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] and [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-total-triangles]. For a distinguished triangle, naturality of $\lambda$ gives its first two arrow squares, and naturality on its last arrow followed by step 5 gives the last-arrow square with the specified shifts. Thus $\lambda$ is an isomorphism of triangulated functors. In particular, let $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ be an equivariant module sequence and $\delta:QC\to QA[1]$ its canonical boundary from [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Its image under $\mathsf K$ has boundary equal to that of the termwise exact Koszul sequence, by the last clause of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-total-triangles]. Therefore
$$\sigma_R R\Gamma(\delta)\lambda_C=\lambda_A[1]\delta_K.$$
The cone convention here is the given negative projection, not a freely chosen sign on the boundary. This is the required connecting-morphism compatibility.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image; agent lattice comparison calculation

proof.text:
For a module $P$ and resolution $s:P[0]\to J$, the actual chain square is $K(s)b_{P[0]}=b_J\Gamma(s)$: both maps place the invariant section's image in $J^0$ in Koszul degree zero. Hence
$$\lambda_P Q(b_{P[0]})=c_s^{-1}Q\Gamma(s)=\eta_{P[0]},$$
where the last equality is naturality of the unit with $c_s=\eta_J^{-1}R\Gamma(Qs)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. This is the canonical invariant-inclusion map on modules, simultaneously for all modules by step 4. When $r=0$, $\Gamma$ and $K$ are both the identity and $b_J=1_J$; the normalized derived-identity computation identifies $L_s$ with $Q(s)^{-1}Q(s)=1$. Finally step 4 applied to $v=Qs$ and to the identity resolution of $J$ gives $\lambda_P=\lambda_J Q(Ks)$ after the canonical resolution identification, as asserted. The zero module and zero ring give only zero objects and identity maps of those objects, so introduce no exceptions.
